answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it votes on reputation or receives shared rewards. The protocol caps each stake’s influence and slashes it when fraud is proven, while honest participants can recover it after a challenge period. Creating a thousand sybils then requires funding a thousand locks and risks losing them all; names like opal, lotus, and glacier do not multiply voting power for free. This raises the attacker’s capital cost, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright.
